visuals: A vast, dry savanna landscape in Senegal with yellow grass and sparse trees under a hot sun.
script: The landscape is a mix of dry, sunny plains.

visuals: Lush green countryside in Senegal during the rainy season from June to October with dark fertile earth and leafy trees.
script: And rainy green zones from June to October. It's warm, breezy, and changes a lot by season, kind of like flipping between summer and spring!

visuals: A wide, peaceful view of the Senegal River with traditional wooden canoes (pirogues) and lush vegetation along the banks.
script: One breathtaking sight is the Senegal River, stretching along the northern border. It’s a major West African waterway full of life and stories.

visuals: A massive, ancient baobab tree with its thick trunk and twisty branches standing alone in a sunny Senegalese landscape.
script: If Senegal had a superhero tree, it would be the baobab, giant trunk, twisty branches, and totally iconic. You’ll find them standing proud all across the country.

visuals: A graceful gazelle sprinting across the dry grassland savanna in Senegal.
script: Gazelles sprint across the sunny savanna.

visuals: A West African manatee swimming just below the surface of a calm river in Senegal.
script: While in the rivers and coastal waters, the rare West African manatee paddles quietly. Nature lovers, this place is gold!

visuals: A vibrant street in Dakar, Senegal, with colorful murals, people in traditional dress, and the Atlantic Ocean in the background.
script: Now, can you guess the capital city? Drumroll… it’s Dakar! Right on the western edge, it’s buzzing with music, fashion, and street food that’ll blow your mind.

visuals: The colorful colonial buildings and narrow streets of Saint-Louis, Senegal, with people walking near the historic bridge.
script: But don’t stop there! Saint-Louis charms with its colorful colonial buildings, bustling markets, and streets full of music, laughter, and the smells of delicious local food.

visuals: The magnificent Great Mosque of Touba in Senegal, with its tall minarets and intricate architecture under a clear sky.
script: and Touba?... That’s a holy city known for its grand mosque and bustling religious markets.

visuals: A quiet, historic street in the Medina of Dakar, Senegal, with its traditional houses and a few locals chatting.
script: Speaking of people, did you know French is the official language? But many folks also chat away in Wolof, Pulaar, and Serer, talk about a language party!

visuals: A pleasant afternoon at the Place de l'Indépendance in Dakar, Senegal, with pedestrians walking near the central gardens and colonial-era buildings.
script: Senegal is home to around 17 million people: that’s about the same as everyone living in the New York City metro area. Busy, friendly, and full of rhythm!

visuals: A large traditional platter of Senegalese Thieboudienne (rice and fish) with colorful vegetables like carrots and eggplant.
script: Now for my favorite part: food! Thieboudienne is a legendary rice and fish dish eaten almost everywhere. Imagine flavors swimming in tomato, onion, and spices. Yum!

visuals: A tall glass of bright red Senegalese bissap (hibiscus drink) with ice cubes and a fresh hibiscus flower.
script: On hot afternoons, people cool down with a red hibiscus drink called bissap. It’s tangy, sweet, and super refreshing. Kind of like summer in a glass.

visuals: A delicious plate of Senegalese Yassa chicken with a rich onion and lemon sauce, served over white rice.
script: And dinner? Let’s make it Yassa chicken! Tender meat soaked in lemony onion sauce. Families love it, and trust me, your nose will find it way before your fork does!

visuals: Senegalese drummers playing traditional sabar drums for a crowd of people dancing mbalax at an outdoor night festival.
script: And get this: at parties, sabar drummers make the ground shake! The music called mbalax mixes ancient beats with pop vibes… People dance like the floor’s on fire.

visuals: A historic image of Senegalese fans celebrating in the streets of Dakar after beating France in the 2002 World Cup.
script:
Remember 2002? Senegal shocked the world by beating then-champions France in their debut men’s World Cup match. 
Fans were jumping in the streets!

visuals: Senegalese soccer star Sadio Mané celebrating a goal in his national team jersey.
script: Besides soccer, traditional wrestling is huge here. Athletes like Sadio Mané are national heroes.

visuals: A traditional Senegalese wrestling match (Laamb) in a sandy arena with a large crowd cheering.
script: And Balla Gaye 2 are national heroes: fast feet, big hearts.

visuals: The stunning pink waters of Lake Retba (Lac Rose) in Senegal, with white salt piles on the shore and a clear blue sky.
script: But wait, there’s more… ever seen a pink lake? Lake Retba shimmers like a strawberry milkshake thanks to special algae and salt. Nature’s magic trick!
